title: Normalized coefficient reduction and total-limit shift data
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a scheme $W$. Use the coefficient calculus $S$, its actual reduction $\mathcal R$, finite derived extensions $F_n$, adjunction $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$, and finite K-flat reduction models of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Use the actual sequence module category, exact restriction $U$ to towers of completed-coefficient modules, and $\mathcal L=R\lim\circ D(U)$ of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Indices $n\in\mathbf N$ denote coefficient exponent $n+1$. Cochain complexes, localization $Q$, and integer shifts have the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; K-flatness and K-injectivity mean [def-pc-kflat-complex] and [def-pur-kinjective-complex].

Define the following data and canonical helper maps, without asserting that the data are inhabited. For a complex $N$ of sequence modules and a quasi-isomorphism $j:U(N)\to I$ to a K-injective tower, let $m_{N,I,j}:\mathcal L(QN)\simeq Q(\lim I)$ be the exact restriction/localization comparison followed by $R\lim(Qj)$ and the right-derived-functor comparison on $I$. For any $j$ and integer $r$, define $j_r:U(N[r])\to I[r]$ by the canonical termwise shift identification followed by $j[r]$. Define $\pi_{I,r}:\prod_n Q((I[r])_n)\simeq(\prod_n Q(I_n))[r]$ by the localization shifts and preservation of products by the shift equivalence. A normalized Roos triangle for $(N,I,j)$ consists of maps $p:\mathcal L(QN)\to\prod_nQ(I_n)$ and $\delta:\prod_nQ(I_n)\to\mathcal L(QN)[1]$ making the Roos triangle for the actual transitions of $I$ distinguished in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit], with $p_n=m_{N,I,j};Q(\lim I\to I_n)$, with diagrammatic composition.

Define normalized reduction/limit shift data for $S$ to consist of: (1) coherent integer-shift structures on $\mathcal R$, every $F_n$, and $\mathcal L$; (2) for every K-flat complex $K$ and K-flat shift $K[r]$, equality of the finite shift comparison with the canonical termwise shift under the specified finite reduction models, and shift compatibility of every actual evaluation identification $\mathcal R(-)_n\simeq F_n(-)$; (3) for every $j$ as above and every $r$ for which $I[r]$ is K-injective and $j_r$ a quasi-isomorphism, equality of the $\mathcal L$ shift comparison with the termwise-limit shift under $m_{N,I,j}$ and $m_{N[r],I[r],j_r}$; (4) countable products in the derived category of completed-coefficient modules and a normalized Roos triangle for every $(N,I,j)$; (5) writing $\sigma_{N,r}:\mathcal L(Q(N[r]))\to\mathcal L(QN)[r]$ for localization shift followed by the supplied limit shift, the equations $p_{N[r],I[r],j_r};\pi_{I,r}=\sigma_{N,r};p_{N,I,j}[r]$ and $\delta_{N[r],I[r],j_r};\sigma_{N,r}[1]=(-1)^r\pi_{I,r};\delta_{N,I,j}[r];\mathrm{comm}_{1,r}$, with semicolons denoting diagrammatic composition; (6) compatibility of the actual adjunction unit and counit with the supplied reduction and limit shifts for every integer $r$.
